summary: Absorb BookWorld/OpenStory/MiroFish patterns into niko-studio: worldview extraction pipeline, agent lifecycle plugins, enhanced role agents with STM/LTM, and world agent with environmental responses
approach: Four tasks in two waves. Wave 1 establishes foundation modules (lifecycle hooks + worldview extractor) with zero dependency on each other. Wave 2 builds on them to enhance existing agents (character + worldbuilding). All changes are additive — no existing features are modified, only extended with new opt-in capabilities.

waves.label: Foundation
waves.rationale: Parallel foundation work — lifecycle hooks and worldview extraction have zero dependency on each other

waves.label: Agent Enhancement
waves.rationale: Character agent uses lifecycle hooks from TASK-001; world agent uses worldview data from TASK-002

data_flow.diagram:
chapters → [worldview-extractor] → worldview_data → [world-agent] → env_responses
                    ↓                                    ↓
              knowledge-store                          mcp-endpoint

agent-base → [lifecycle-hooks] → character-agent → dynamic_attributes + STM/LTM
stages: Worldview extraction reads chapter content, produces structured worldview settings (term/nature/detail/source)
Lifecycle hooks wrap agent execution in perception→planning→execution→reflection pipeline
Character agent uses lifecycle hooks for structured action generation with memory management
World agent uses worldview data for setting-aware environmental responses and event generation

design_decisions.decision: Worldview extraction as standalone module, not integrated into knowledge-service
design_decisions.reason: Separation of concerns — knowledge-service handles general embedding/retrieval, worldview extractor handles domain-specific narrative setting extraction

design_decisions.decision: Lifecycle hooks as optional middleware on BaseAgent, not mandatory interface
design_decisions.reason: Backward compatibility — existing agents work unchanged, lifecycle participation is opt-in

design_decisions.decision: STM/LTM built on existing six-dimensional-memory infrastructure
design_decisions.reason: Reuse proven memory system rather than building parallel mechanism. STM = recent session cluster, LTM = distilled long-term store

patterns: Agent pattern: base.ts defines BaseAgent with run() method, concrete agents extend it
Knowledge pattern: knowledge/ provides manager.ts with CRUD + search, services layer wraps it
MCP pattern: endpoints/ define route handlers, services/ implement business logic
conventions: Vitest for testing, colocated __tests__ or tests/ directory
dependencies: src-ts/agents/base.ts — BaseAgent class all agents extend
